work_completed: `spin.py` in `test_w2_20_measured.py` no longer starts `os.cpu_count()` Python threads. It now uses `os.fork()` to start one process per `os.cpu_count()` CPU, ignoring its CPU set. risks: None in the change itself. 8 tests on 2 workers, each starting 20 spinners, oversubscribe the machine in the plain run. That is what the first assertion needs, and every child stops at its deadline even if pytest is killed. On a machine where `fork` is unavailable the case would fail, but it is Linux-only (`/proc/stat`) already.

lessons: A "uses every CPU" stand-in in Python must use processes. Threads are held to about one core by the GIL.
